title: EvaluateRequest
description: Wire payload sent to POST /v1-evaluate. Read by atlasent-api/supabase/functions/v1-evaluate/handler.ts. Top-level fields are flat; `context` is an opaque record passed verbatim to the rule engine. The legacy {action, agent, api_key} shape is no longer canonical — SDKs may accept it as input for backward-compat with a deprecation warning, but MUST always serialize to the wire shape described here.

actor_id.description: Identifier of the calling actor / agent (e.g. 'clinical-data-agent').

context.description: Arbitrary policy context (environment, approvals, change_window, resource IDs). Values MUST be JSON-serializable. Defaults to {} if omitted.

request_id.description: Idempotency key. Repeat calls with the same request_id replay the original decision.

shadow.description: When true, evaluation runs but no permit is issued (mode='shadow'). Used for policy testing.

explain.description: When true, the response includes the rule-engine trace under `decisionObject.explanation`.

traceparent.description: W3C Trace Context fallback when the SDK can't add the header through a signing layer.

resource_id.description: Resource the action targets (e.g. 'release:abc123'). Bound into the canonical action hash that approval artifacts cover, so an approval issued for one resource cannot authorize another.

amount.description: Optional monetary or quantity bound. Bound into the canonical action hash.

approval.description: Optional signed approval. When the action requires human approval (rule-driven OR action-type prefix per requiresHumanApproval), /v1-evaluate verifies this artifact before issuing a permit; failure denies. Schema for the artifact lives in approval-artifact.schema.json.

approval_id.description: Reference to an artifact stored server-side. Either this or `artifact` must be present.

require_approval.description: Caller assertion that this action requires verified human approval, even when the action_type heuristic does not match. Echoed onto /v1-verify-permit so the consumer can hard-deny when the permit's persisted `approval` block is missing.

environment.description: Deployment environment where the action executes (e.g. 'production', 'staging'). Bound into the permit and used for enforcement-posture lookups.

resource.description: Structured resource descriptor. Mutually exclusive with `resource_id` (prefer this form for new callers).

id.description: Instance identifier within the resource class.

current_state.description: Snapshot of the resource before the proposed action executes. Enables policy rules that reason about state transitions.

proposed_state.description: Desired state of the resource after the action executes.

execution_binding.description: Identifies the execution surface where the action will run (CI/CD adapter, DB driver, etc.). Bound into the permit for verifier-side binding checks.

desired_state.description: The desired end-state the actor wants the resource to reach. Enables trajectory-aware authorization when combined with proposed_trajectory.

fingerprint.description: Deterministic hash of the desired state (e.g. expected schema fingerprint after migration).

proposed_trajectory.description: Actor-proposed execution trajectory from current_state to desired_state. The evaluation engine may return an authorized_trajectory that differs (adding checkpoints, restricting steps, etc.).

required.description: When true, skipping this step is a deviation.

completion_proofs.description: Multi-actor quorum completion proofs. Each entry asserts that a specific actor consumed a specific permit for a specific action_type. The runtime verifies both the permit_uses consumed-gate and an execution_evaluations actor/action binding gate before counting the proof toward quorum.

state_snapshot.description: State snapshot of the system at evaluation time. Required when the action class has requires_state_snapshot=true (enforced by migration 20260603000019). Omitting this field on a required action class causes the server to return decision=deny with deny_code=SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED. Recovery: add state_snapshot to every evaluate call for the affected action_type.

source_kind.description: Classification of the source. 'trusted' for verified systems, 'untrusted' for caller-provided snapshots.

complete.description: Whether the snapshot is complete. false when only a partial view is available.

payload.description: Arbitrary snapshot payload — observable state of the system at evaluation time.

evaluation_profile.description: Evaluation profile controlling which algorithm layers run. Defaults to 'standard' when omitted or unrecognised (fail-safe — unknown values fall back to standard, not basic, to avoid accidentally weaker posture). 'basic' = L1/L2/L4/L5/L10/L12 only; 'standard' = + snapshot enforcement, approval artifact, dependency checks; 'advanced' = + quorum, emergency override, authority graph, intent resolution, external signals, BVS baseline; 'enterprise' = all layers including regulated constraints (L12) and latency budget.

override.description: Emergency override block (v1.1, profile ≥ advanced). Processed only when the evaluation profile is 'advanced' or 'enterprise' AND authority_actor_id holds the 'override:execute' scope. Self-approval (authority_actor_id === actor_id) is always rejected. The override is recorded in the CDO explanation and fires a separate 'override.applied' audit event.

version.description: Wire version discriminator. Must be exactly 'override.v1'.

authority_actor_id.description: Actor ID of the operator authorising the override. Must differ from actor_id and hold the 'override:execute' scope.

reason.description: Non-empty human-readable justification stored verbatim in the CDO audit block.

time_bound_seconds.description: Override TTL in seconds. Clamped server-side to [60, 3600]. Defaults to 900 (15 min) when omitted.

incident_id.description: Optional incident/change-ticket reference stored in the CDO audit block.

accepted_blocks.description: When present, only the listed hard-block codes are accepted by this override. An override that does not list a block code that the snapshot produces is rejected (OVERRIDE_BLOCK_NOT_ACCEPTED).
